## Definitions

- [statement] Mirabegron is not free of autonomic safety considerations: the urogenital review lists worsening hypertension and urinary retention among potential adverse effects, and PaDoMi reported an acute urinary-retention case. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33389776/
- [statement] Rotigotine is not an established apathy treatment: the 2019 MDS review rated it unlikely efficacious, and a later placebo-controlled study in drug-naive PD also missed its apathy primary outcome. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7738499/
- [statement] CBT is a supported option for anxiety in PD, but outcomes depend on the scale: the 2021 randomized trial improved the Parkinson Anxiety Scale relative to monitoring while the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale difference was not significant. The 2024 German guideline recommends offering CBT for anxiety. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9290129/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] CBT-I is a preferred behavioral approach to insomnia, but PD-specific efficacy and implementation should be described cautiously: the computerized ACCORD-PD trial showed better insomnia scores among completers, yet its intention-to-treat comparison was not significant and treatment dropout was high. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/

## How it works

- [statement] The German guideline publication in 2024 advises considering competing causes of cognitive impairment, including vitamin deficiencies and metabolic disorders, and reviewing medications with anticholinergic cognitive effects. ## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The cited review describes screening for orthostatic hypotension with supine blood pressure and heart rate followed by measurements after 3 minutes standing, and defines it as a systolic fall ≥20 mmHg and/or diastolic fall ≥10 mmHg; it also mentions a longer standing challenge when delayed hypotension is suspected. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] SIAXI randomized 184 adults, including 70.7% with PD, to placebo or incobotulinumtoxinA 75 U or 100 U; the 100 U group improved salivary flow and patient global impression at week 4, with a lasting effect at week 16. These are mixed-population results. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The ACCORD-PD pilot found greater insomnia improvement among computerized CBT-I completers than education completers, but not in intention-to-treat analysis; dropout in the CBT-I group was 43%. Adherence limits generalizability. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The 2020 review recommends slow position changes, avoiding heat and large carbohydrate-rich meals, and stepwise nonpharmacological treatment; water and salt supplementation require caution in heart, kidney or liver failure. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE’s 2017 recommendations place fludrocortisone after midodrine when it is contraindicated, intolerable or ineffective and emphasize cardiac risk; the 2020 review additionally highlights hypokalemia monitoring and contraindications in heart or kidney failure. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/
- [statement] Non-drug orthostatic measures include standing slowly, avoiding heat and large carbohydrate-rich meals, and individualized water and salt intake. Supplementation requires caution with heart, kidney or liver failure; abdominal binders have better supporting evidence than compression stockings in the cited review. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2017 NICE PD recommendations advise considering midodrine with monitoring for supine hypertension, followed by consideration of fludrocortisone when midodrine is contraindicated, ineffective or not tolerated; cardiac risks and interactions matter. The OH review also warns of heart or kidney failure and hypokalemia with fludrocortisone. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/
- [statement] The cited sources note that treating upright hypotension requires attention to supine and nocturnal hypertension, which can coexist and limit pressor treatment, and that blood-pressure monitoring is part of management. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] The cited sources distinguish PD-MCI, where functional independence is preserved despite possible subtle difficulty with complex tasks, from Parkinson’s disease dementia, where cognitive impairment interferes with daily activities; motor disability alone does not establish dementia. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073727/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] NICE NG71 (2017) recommends offering a cholinesterase inhibitor for mild or moderate Parkinson’s disease dementia and considering one for severe dementia; the severe-dementia recommendation has weaker wording. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE recommends speech and language therapy for Parkinson’s disease when communication, swallowing or saliva problems occur; therapy includes swallowing safety strategies such as EMST and effort-based speech strategies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE recommends considering medication for drooling when non-drug management is unavailable or ineffective, considering glycopyrronium bromide and specialist referral for botulinum toxin A. It restricts other anticholinergics to people judged at minimal cognitive-adverse-effect risk. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE advises considering augmentative and alternative communication equipment as Parkinson’s disease progresses and communication needs change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] SIAXI’s population was 70.7% PD, so its overall results are not PD-only estimates. Treatment-related dry mouth occurred in 5.4% and 2.7%, and dysphagia in 2.7% and 0.0%, of the 75 U and 100 U groups respectively; these findings do not imply swallowing risk is absent. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE NG71 says not to offer olanzapine for PD psychosis, and the 2019 MDS review rated it not efficacious with unacceptable risk. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] In the six-week phase 3 pimavanserin trial, SAPS-PD improved more than with placebo without observed motor worsening; adverse-event discontinuations were more frequent with pimavanserin, so the trial does not establish risk-free treatment. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24183563/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline recommends clinical history alongside screening scales: depression cannot be diagnosed from a score alone because PD and affective symptoms overlap. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] A neuropathy review describes multiple potential contributors in people with PD, including genetic disorders, treatment effects and concomitant disease; its diagnostic approach includes history, clinical examination, blood tests and nerve-conduction studies. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847250/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] PD sleep complaints require separate assessment of insomnia, REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), and excessive daytime sleepiness; results on overall sleep quality should not be assumed to establish efficacy for each phenotype. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13612690/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7111581/
- [statement] The September 2026 phenotype-stratified meta-analysis concluded that pharmacological evidence for PD daytime sleepiness, insomnia and RBD remained insufficient for definitive recommendations; very high heterogeneity made pooled estimates for those domains exploratory. Improvement in overall sleep quality must not be substituted for proof of a specific sleep-disorder benefit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13612690/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] PD constipation can combine slow intestinal transit with outlet obstruction caused by impaired sphincter or puborectalis coordination; assessment should distinguish these mechanisms rather than treating every case as infrequent bowel movements alone. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7774928/
- [statement] A randomized trial of a particular multistrain probiotic preparation reported improved bowel frequency and transit time over 8 weeks; that result supports the tested preparation and duration rather than interchangeable efficacy of all probiotic products. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7774928/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The urogenital review recommends history, bladder diary, urinalysis and post-void residual assessment, with further testing guided by findings to identify coexisting urological disease rather than attributing all urinary symptoms to PD. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The cited sources note that antimuscarinic bladder treatments can worsen constipation, a trade-off relevant to urinary urgency in a person with PD who already has bowel symptoms. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/
- [statement] Mirabegron results differ by study and endpoint: PaDoMi reported improved overactive-bladder symptom scores at Weeks 4 and 8 in a Parkinsonism population, whereas MAESTRO did not achieve its primary composite symptom endpoint when mirabegron was added to behavioral modification including pelvic floor exercises. These are differing study results, rather than proof of universal benefit or no benefit. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33389776/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/
- [statement] In the 2004 placebo-controlled PD dementia trial, 541 patients were enrolled; rivastigmine was studied for 24 weeks and produced moderate benefits. ADAS-cog improved by 2.1 points with rivastigmine versus worsening by 0.7 points with placebo. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2004 PD dementia trial reported nausea in 29.0 percent versus 11.2 percent, vomiting in 16.6 percent versus 1.7 percent, and tremor in 10.2 percent versus 3.9 percent with rivastigmine versus placebo, respectively. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The cited sources describe assessing cognitive complaints using patient and care-partner history plus cognitive testing; a brief global screen such as MoCA can support an abbreviated assessment, while comprehensive neuropsychological assessment evaluates individual domains rather than relying only on one global score. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073727/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] Rivastigmine offers modest symptomatic cognitive benefit in Parkinson’s disease dementia. In the 24-week placebo-controlled trial, mean ADAS-cog improved by 2.1 points with rivastigmine versus a 0.7-point worsening with placebo; this trial result does not establish prevention of dementia progression. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] Cognitive training has mixed evidence: the German guideline supports it for PD-MCI but notes small, heterogeneous trials; an eight-week computerized-training RCT in PD patients with subjective cognitive complaints found no benefit on primary planning accuracy and no group differences at follow-up. The populations and interventions differ, so this is a limitation on generalization rather than proof that every training program fails. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35248830/
- [statement] In the 2010 blinded sham-controlled trial, 60 participants with PD completed four weeks of EMST or sham training; active EMST improved videofluoroscopic penetration–aspiration scores and hyolaryngeal function compared with sham. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The rimabotulinumtoxinB trial describes neurological sialorrhea, including PD, as usually reflecting inefficient elimination of oral saliva rather than increased saliva production. (low confidence) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurol/articlepdf/10.1001/jamaneurol.2019.4565 · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] In PD COMM (2024), LSVT LOUD reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points and versus NHS speech and language therapy by 9.6 points; NHS therapy showed no evidence of benefit over no therapy in this trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Evidence appraisal differs by level: Troche’s trial reported improved swallowing safety after EMST, whereas Gandhi and Steele’s systematic review characterized intervention evidence as low certainty and found that lower-risk-of-bias studies supported efficiency benefits rather than safety benefits. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9159671/
- [statement] In PD COMM, 388 people with PD and dysarthria were randomized. LSVT LOUD used four 50-minute sessions weekly for four weeks plus home practice, and reduced self-reported voice handicap at three months versus no therapy by 8.0 points (99% confidence interval −13.3 to −2.6). (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] PD COMM found no evidence of voice-handicap benefit for the trial’s NHS speech and language therapy arm versus no therapy. It recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events; the trial was unblinded and used a self-reported primary outcome. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The sialorrhea review attributes PD drooling mainly to impaired saliva clearance and reduced swallowing rather than increased saliva production; cited sialometry studies found reduced production relative to people without PD. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6651/12/11/691 · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The SIAXI trial, which included adults with PD and other neurological conditions, found incobotulinumtoxinA 100 U improved salivary flow and patient global change versus placebo at week 4, with effects observed at week 16. NICE supports specialist consideration of botulinum toxin A for drooling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] In the 2012 multicenter placebo-controlled depression trial, paroxetine and venlafaxine XR improved depressive symptoms without worsening motor function; this describes that trial rather than proving all SSRIs effective in PD. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3324323/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Apathy involves diminished motivation and goal-directed behavior and can occur independently of depression; its characteristic indifference differs from depressive dysphoria or hopelessness, despite overlap between the syndromes. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12261265/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7738499/
- [statement] Venlafaxine XR reduced depressive symptoms versus placebo in the 12-week SAD-PD trial without worsening motor function; the 2019 MDS review rates venlafaxine clinically useful for PD depressive symptoms. This establishes trial and review findings, not comparative superiority over all antidepressants. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3324323/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline says physical interventions might be offered for apathy, but its evidence discussion describes small mixed trials, including no significant dance-therapy effect versus active controls. Apathy exercise evidence is less established than a broad efficacy claim would imply. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] PD fatigue is a subjective lack of energy that interferes with function; it differs from sleepiness and from objectively measured muscle fatigability. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4883681/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.parkinson.org/library/fact-sheets/fatigue, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/
- [statement] A review of Parkinson-related peripheral neuropathy lists diabetes, thyroid disease and B12 deficiency among acquired causes; sensory complaints therefore warrant assessment for peripheral neuropathy rather than automatic attribution to central PD pathology. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847250/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Rotigotine showed numerical pain improvement in an exploratory placebo-controlled pilot, but the primary pain comparison was not statistically significant; MDS classified its PD pain use as investigational rather than established efficacy. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26626320/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] A single-center sham-controlled trial of motor-cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation reported a favorable musculoskeletal-pain signal in PD; its small sample and short follow-up support a preliminary adjunctive-treatment claim rather than broad efficacy across PD pain types. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32980772/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2020 pain review distinguishes musculoskeletal, dystonic, nerve, primary and akathitic pain in PD; the heterogeneous pain presentation supports syndrome-specific assessment rather than a single analgesic strategy. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2035-8377/12/3/14 · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] A 2023 systematic review searching trials through May 2021 found a small fatigue benefit from physical exercise across eight trials, but called for further efficacy research and differentiation of physical versus mental fatigue outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] In that 2023 review, pooled modafinil trials did not show a significant fatigue benefit versus placebo, and acupuncture did not show a significant advantage over sham acupuncture; these comparisons should not be presented as proven PD-fatigue therapies. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10473113/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE recommends considering clonazepam or melatonin for PD-related RBD after reviewing medication causes; the 2023 AASM guideline conditionally suggests clonazepam and specifically immediate-release melatonin for secondary RBD. These are conditional treatment options rather than proof that every formulation works. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] In a placebo-controlled trial of thirty people with PD-RBD, prolonged-release melatonin 4 mg did not reduce RBD events; the primary endpoint comparison was not significant (P = 0.92). This finding concerns that formulation and trial, rather than disproving all melatonin regimens. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674060/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] A negative prolonged-release melatonin trial should not be presented as a test of immediate-release melatonin: in 30 PD patients, 4 mg prolonged-release melatonin over 8 weeks did not reduce RBD compared with placebo, while AASM separately conditionally recommends immediate-release melatonin and finds insufficient evidence for prolonged-release melatonin in secondary RBD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7027846/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/
- [statement] In the ACCORD-PD pilot, 28 participants were recruited; completion was 8/14 with computerized CBT-I versus 13/14 with standard education. Insomnia Severity Index improvement favored CBT-I among completers (−7.9 versus −3.5), but the intention-to-treat comparison was not significant (p = 0.48). (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5568719/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Modafinil is a conditional clinical option rather than a reliably effective treatment for every sleepy PD patient: NICE says to consider it after excluding reversible causes, but a placebo-controlled trial of 40 patients found no significant improvement in subjective Epworth sleepiness or objective multiple sleep latency testing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1739456/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The cited sources describe assessing reversible contributors to OH and reviewing medicines that lower blood pressure, including antihypertensive and dopaminergic treatments, before escalating symptom-directed treatment. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] The cited sources state that midodrine can be considered for PD-related OH, with attention to contraindications and supine hypertension; they describe supine and home blood-pressure monitoring as helping to balance upright benefit against hypertension while lying down. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated droxidopa efficacious only in the short term and possibly useful, while rating the PD-specific efficacy evidence for midodrine and fludrocortisone insufficient; prescribing recommendations should not be mistaken for strong long-term PD trial evidence. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Macrogol has placebo-controlled evidence for PD constipation and was rated likely efficacious and possibly useful in the 2019 MDS review. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] In the placebo-controlled lubiprostone trial, short-term constipation improvement favored active treatment, while intermittent loose stools were the most common reported adverse event. These findings do not establish long-term comparative effectiveness. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22573627/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review called probiotics with prebiotic fiber efficacious and clinically useful on the basis of one trial; the 2022 meta-analysis instead concluded that evidence remained insufficient, noting few trials, heterogeneous preparations and high heterogeneity. These are attributed assessments with different evidence sets, not an unconditional endorsement of probiotics. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9684193/
- [statement] Mirabegron bladder-trial findings differ: PaDoMi reported improved OAB symptom scores and another placebo-controlled PD trial reported positive primary outcomes, whereas MAESTRO found no significant primary composite-score benefit from adding mirabegron to behavioral modification. Results should be interpreted by population, comparator and endpoint. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33389776/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34672847/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/
- [statement] For refractory detrusor overactivity, the urogenital review describes intradetrusor botulinum toxin as an option but explicitly warns about urinary retention. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The cited sources state that orthostatic hypotension in PD should prompt review of blood-pressure-lowering medicines and correction of reversible contributors such as dehydration, and that it should not automatically be attributed solely to neurodegeneration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] Macrogol and lubiprostone have supportive PD constipation trial evidence, but this should be described with the limits of small, short studies. The 2019 MDS review classified both as likely efficacious and possibly useful; the 2018 constipation review cautioned against strong recommendations from the evidence then available. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] Antimuscarinic treatment for overactive bladder in PD requires attention to worsening constipation and cognitive adverse effects; the MAESTRO investigators describe these as reasons to study alternatives. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Bladder treatment evidence includes important selection and safety limits: MAESTRO excluded patients with excessive post-void residual and evidence of urinary tract infection; PaDoMi reported a mild rise in residual urine and one episode of acute urinary retention. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33389776/
- [statement] Assessment combines patient and informant history with cognitive testing. MDS Level I is abbreviated; Level II uses comprehensive testing across five cognitive domains, with two tests per domain. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073727/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] Rivastigmine has the strongest established drug evidence for PD dementia: the 2019 MDS review rates it efficacious and clinically useful, and the 2024 German guideline recommends its use. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review classifies rivastigmine for nondementia cognitive impairment as investigational with insufficient evidence; the 2024 German guideline recommends against rivastigmine, donepezil, galantamine and memantine for PD-MCI. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] A 28-participant PD-MCI rivastigmine patch crossover trial found a nonsignificant trend on its global primary outcome and no treatment effect on cognitive measures; a positive secondary everyday-cognition measure does not establish broad cognitive efficacy. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25914281/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] Donepezil has weaker evidence than rivastigmine in PD dementia: MDS in 2019 retained insufficient efficacy evidence but rated it possibly useful, while the 2024 German guideline permits possible off-label use. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline says cognitive training can be offered for PD-MCI and cognitive stimulation can be offered for PD dementia; these are distinct interventions tailored to different levels of cognitive impairment. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline recommends aerobic training for PD-MCI, while explaining that the suggested schedule is based on expert consensus and the optimal intensity and frequency have not been established. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Cognitive training should not be presented as proven durable prevention: a PD-MCI trial reported memory benefit at six months but not twelve, while a separate broader PD trial found no cognitive advantage or difference in conversion of cognitive status at one or two years. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563628/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10724826/
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline advises against using food supplements or herbal therapeutics to treat cognitive deficits in PD-MCI or PD dementia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Galantamine recommendations also differ by guideline and date: the 2019 MDS review calls it possibly useful despite insufficient PD dementia efficacy evidence; the 2024 German guideline recommends against its use. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] A 2021 clinical review recommends evaluating reversible contributors before attributing all cognitive change to PD, including anticholinergic drugs, benzodiazepines, opioids, and metabolic or nutritional contributors assessed through appropriate laboratory testing. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073727/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Rivastigmine’s cognitive benefit must be balanced against tolerability: its dementia trial found more nausea, vomiting and tremor than placebo, and the German guideline also recognizes tremor and worsening PD symptoms as adverse effects. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] Dementia drug evidence should not be extrapolated to PD-MCI. The 2024 German guideline recommends against rivastigmine, donepezil, galantamine and memantine for PD-MCI; the 2021 review likewise found no effective pharmacologic treatment for PD-MCI. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073727/
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline recommends rivastigmine for PDD and says donepezil might be used off label; it does not regard all cholinesterase inhibitors as equally supported. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] For PDD, the German guideline says cognitive stimulation can be offered and reminiscence therapy might be offered; it distinguishes these approaches from targeted cognitive training for PD-MCI. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The dysphagia consensus recommends instrumental assessment to guide treatment; the management review recommends video fluoroscopy or video endoscopy in severe PD to adjust food and liquid consistency. (medium confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040 · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995701/
- [statement] Short-term swallowing improvements should not be interpreted as establishing comparative or durable superiority of dysphagia therapies: the 2020 systematic review found insufficient evidence to compare techniques, and the 2021 consensus found the treatment literature mainly Class IV. (medium confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/17/11/4104 · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040
- [statement] Dopaminergic medication does not reliably normalize swallowing: the management review states that swallowing does not necessarily improve, while the dysphagia consensus describes antiparkinsonian drug effects as controversial. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995701/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022510X21027040
- [statement] Botulinum toxin A and B have treatment evidence for PD drooling: the 2019 MDS review rated both efficacious and clinically useful with specialized monitoring, while SIAXI demonstrated benefit of incobotulinumtoxinA in a mixed neurological population that included PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/
- [statement] PD COMM recorded 93 adverse events with LSVT LOUD and 46 with NHS speech and language therapy, predominantly vocal strain, with no serious adverse events. Most participants had early PD and mild speech impairment; allocation was unblinded and participant or carer expectations could bias questionnaire outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] In a sham-controlled randomized trial, 60 participants completed four weeks of EMST or sham training; EMST improved penetration–aspiration scores and hyolaryngeal function. NICE includes EMST among swallowing safety strategies. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] The EMST trial mainly enrolled people with mild to moderate swallowing impairment; its authors explicitly stated that prevention of aspiration pneumonia, durability and maintenance requirements still needed study. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] NICE NG71 recommends leaving well-tolerated hallucinations and delusions untreated; potentially triggering Parkinson medicines should be reduced only with specialist advice and consideration of symptom severity and withdrawal effects. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated clozapine and pimavanserin clinically useful for PD psychosis; the 2024 systematic review of reviews also identified these two agents as having the strongest efficacy and tolerability evidence. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11505035/
- [statement] Quetiapine should not be described as having established placebo-controlled efficacy for PD psychosis: the 2019 MDS review rated evidence insufficient and practice implications possibly useful; NICE NG71 nevertheless says to consider it in patients without cognitive impairment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] CBT has supportive evidence for PD depression: the 2019 MDS review rated it likely efficacious and possibly useful, while a 2024 meta-analysis found reductions in depression and anxiety; blinding constraints and the need for longer follow-up qualify confidence. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11470855/
- [statement] In the 48-participant anxiety CBT trial, CBT did not significantly outperform clinical monitoring on the primary Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale endpoint, although it improved the PD-specific Parkinson Anxiety Scale; benefit should be described as outcome-dependent. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9290129/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The absence of eligible anxiety trials in the 2019 MDS review is a historical search result, not a current claim that no PD anxiety RCTs exist: a later randomized CBT study reported both a nonsignificant general anxiety endpoint and benefit on a PD-specific scale. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9290129/
- [statement] Apathy drug evidence is restricted: the 2019 MDS review based rivastigmine possibly-useful status on one small positive study, and piribedil possibly-useful status applied specifically after subthalamic stimulation and dopamine-agonist withdrawal. These findings should not be generalized to every patient with apathy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] A small retrospective psychosis cohort found no statistically significant mortality difference between pimavanserin and quetiapine; retrospective design, mixed PD/Lewy-body-dementia enrollment, concomitant treatment and limited power prevent concluding equivalent mortality safety. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7061324/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Apathy is reduced motivation and goal-directed thinking or action; it can occur independently of depression. The 2024 German guideline stresses that distinguishing apathy from depressive affect is clinically challenging. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] Pimavanserin improved PD psychosis in the placebo-controlled phase 3 trial without worsening motor function. The 2019 MDS review judged short-term efficacy sufficient for a clinically useful rating, while explicitly noting the limited controlled safety evidence beyond six weeks available to that review. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24183563/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] CBT is supported for depressive symptoms in PD. The 2019 MDS review rated it likely efficacious and possibly useful while noting blinding and adverse-event-reporting limitations; the 2024 German guideline recommends offering CBT. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/
- [statement] Apathy drug evidence is limited: the 2019 MDS review based its rivastigmine efficacy conclusion on one small positive high-quality trial and therefore rated the practice implication only possibly useful. This is not evidence for routine treatment of every patient with apathy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease non-motor symptoms: neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review scoped its positive piribedil apathy conclusion to patients after subthalamic nucleus stimulation and initial dopamine-agonist withdrawal; it rated rotigotine unlikely efficacious after a negative high-quality apathy trial, despite post hoc signals. Within-group improvement should not be presented as treatment-specific efficacy. - [statement] Small experimental studies found that levodopa can increase pain thresholds in PD. These laboratory threshold results should be distinguished from demonstrated relief of chronic clinical pain. - [statement] Experimental findings on sensory thresholds conflict: one study reported that thermal and mechanical pain thresholds were uninfluenced by levodopa or STN-DBS, whereas another reported significant increases in mechanical pain and tolerance thresholds after acute STN-DBS and after acute levodopa administration. A uniform direct effect on central pain processing is not established by these studies. ## Research summary — PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder

This section covers Parkinson’s autonomic symptoms: orthostatic hypotension, constipation and bladder symptoms. OH management combines medication review and nonpharmacological measures with selected drugs while monitoring supine hypertension. Constipation can involve slow transit and impaired evacuation; macrogol and lubiprostone have trial support. The cited review describes bladder assessment as checking coexisting urological disease and medication trade-offs. Antimuscarinics may worsen constipation, while mirabegron trials have differing outcomes. Probiotic recommendations also differ across evidence reviews; product-specific and short-term results should retain their qualifications.

## Source disagreement — PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder

The 2019 MDS review called probiotics with prebiotic fiber efficacious and clinically useful on the basis of one trial; the 2022 meta-analysis instead concluded that evidence remained insufficient, noting few trials, heterogeneous preparations and high heterogeneity. These are attributed assessments with different evidence sets, not an unconditional endorsement of probiotics.

## Source disagreement — PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder

Mirabegron bladder-trial findings differ: PaDoMi reported improved OAB symptom scores and another placebo-controlled PD trial reported positive primary outcomes, whereas MAESTRO found no significant primary composite-score benefit from adding mirabegron to behavioral modification. Results should be interpreted by population, comparator and endpoint.

## Research summary — PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment

PD cognitive treatment depends on whether functional independence is preserved or cognition impairs daily activities. Rivastigmine has the strongest established drug evidence for PD dementia, with moderate benefits and tolerability trade-offs. Dementia drug results should not be generalized to PD-MCI. Cognitive training, stimulation and aerobic activity have different roles and evidence limits; durable prevention of cognitive decline remains unproven. Guideline recommendations for memantine and galantamine differ and require attribution to the issuing guideline and date.

## Source disagreement — PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment

Memantine recommendations differ: NICE NG71 (2017) allows consideration only when cholinesterase inhibitors are contraindicated or not tolerated, whereas the 2024 German guideline recommends against memantine for PD dementia.

## Source disagreement — PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment

Cognitive training has mixed evidence: the German guideline supports it for PD-MCI but notes small, heterogeneous trials; an eight-week computerized-training RCT in PD patients with subjective cognitive complaints found no benefit on primary planning accuracy and no group differences at follow-up. The populations and interventions differ, so this is a limitation on generalization rather than proof that every training program fails.

## Research summary — PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems

The cited sources describe specialist assessment and targeted treatment for PD swallowing, saliva and communication problems. Swallowing impairment can cause aspiration pneumonia and nutritional harm; instrumental assessment guides management. EMST has short-term swallowing trial evidence, but comparative and long-term dysphagia treatment evidence remains limited. Botulinum toxin has randomized evidence for drooling, with dry mouth and dysphagia reported as adverse events. LSVT LOUD improved participant-reported voice handicap in PD COMM, although vocal strain and trial design limit interpretation. Speech and language therapy also addresses communication strategies and changing equipment needs.

## Research summary — PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

The cited sources treat PD psychosis, depression, anxiety and apathy as distinct problems with distinct assessment and treatment choices. Psychosis care includes checking medical and medication triggers; clozapine and pimavanserin have stronger efficacy evidence than quetiapine. Depression has antidepressant and CBT trial evidence. Anxiety CBT results depend partly on the outcome scale. Apathy can occur independently of depression, and treatment findings from small or selected populations need careful qualification. These distinctions matter because apparent benefit in one syndrome or short trial does not establish benefit or long-term safety across all four.

## Research summary — PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms

Pain, fatigue and sensory disturbances contribute to disability in Parkinson’s disease. The cited sources characterize pain by syndrome; sensory symptoms can involve peripheral neuropathy as well as altered perception. Fatigue is distinct from sleepiness; Parkinson’s Foundation guidance describes assessing other causes, pacing activity and regular exercise. Treatment evidence is uneven: historical MDS ratings are qualified, PANDA and OXYDOPA did not establish their primary analgesic benefits, and sham-controlled acupuncture studies did not show a fatigue-specific advantage. Laboratory changes in pain thresholds should not be equated with durable clinical pain relief. Preliminary stimulation studies remain specific to the pain types and follow-up studied.

## Source disagreement — PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms

Experimental findings on sensory thresholds conflict: one study reported that thermal and mechanical pain thresholds were uninfluenced by levodopa or STN-DBS, whereas another reported significant increases in mechanical pain and tolerance thresholds after acute STN-DBS and after acute levodopa administration. A uniform direct effect on central pain processing is not established by these studies.

## Research summary — PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness

The cited sources distinguish dream enactment with injury risk, insomnia, and daytime sleepiness in PD. The AASM guideline pairs environmental safety advice with conditional drug options for RBD; clonazepam and immediate-release melatonin have conditional guideline support, while prolonged-release melatonin failed in a small PD trial. Insomnia assessment considers other sleep disorders, and CBT-I evidence in PD is promising but limited by small studies and adherence. NICE describes a medication review, a search for reversible causes and driving precautions for daytime sleepiness. Modafinil has mixed efficacy evidence; CPAP evidence applies to coexisting obstructive sleep apnea. Guideline options and positive pooled findings should retain their evidence limitations.
